title: Settings card: 2024 Kawasaki KX250
ig_caption:
2024 Kawasaki KX250. About 185 lb, fast, hardpack moto, stability and jump support the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the stock settings from the 2024 KX250 owner's manual.

Stock is 11 on fork comp and 12 on fork rebound, 12 clicks and 1 1/2 turns on the shock, 13 on shock rebound. Dialed opened fork comp one click, slowed fork rebound one, went two clicks in on low-speed and set sag at 103 mm. Everything counted out from fully closed.

These are starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time. Ride it, log how it felt, move one thing.

title: Settings card: 2025 KTM 500 EXC-F
ig_caption:
2025 KTM 500 EXC-F. About 205 lb, fast, rocks and roots, stability and grip the goals. Left is stock from the 2025 KTM owner's manual for the 450 and 500 EXC-F, right is the baseline Dialed built for that rider.

Fork comp 15 to 12, fork rebound 17 to 12. Shock low-speed 15 to 10, high-speed 2 turns to 1 1/2, rebound 15 to 12. Sag stays at the manual's 110 mm. A heavier, faster rider gets more support and slower rebound on both ends to keep the big four-stroke settled over the rocks.

All clicks counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

title: Comment answer: why the app asks where you ride
ig_caption:
Someone asked in the comments why the app wants to know their location. Fair question.

It's optional, and your clicker settings don't use it. It fills in your state and riding region and suggests which track you're at when you log a ride day. Skip it and your starting point comes out the same: built from your bike, weight, skill and terrain, then refined on the bike one change at a time.

title: Settings card: 2023 Kawasaki KX450
ig_caption:
2023 Kawasaki KX450. About 200 lb, intermediate, hardpack, sand and dunes, stability and comfort at speed the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the stock settings from the 2023 KX450 owner's manual.

Stock is 14 and 12 on the fork, 18 on shock low-speed, 12 on shock rebound. Dialed went two clicks in on fork comp, two out on fork rebound, eight in on low-speed and set sag at 105 mm. Eight clicks is a big move, so if it feels harsh, come back toward stock two at a time.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

Dunes or hardpack: where does your KX450 feel worst?
